heading: Direct vs Regular Mutual Funds: Understanding SEBI’s New Default Plan Rule
tldr: Regular mutual funds involve a distributor who earns a commission, leading to a higher expense ratio for investors.
Direct mutual funds have no distributor commission, resulting in a lower expense ratio and potentially higher returns.
SEBI has introduced guidelines for Execution-Only Platforms (EOPs) to facilitate transactions solely in direct mutual fund plans.
The new framework encourages investors to opt for direct plans by making them the default choice on these EOPs.
Switching from regular to direct plans can significantly boost your long-term wealth accumulation due to lower costs.
caption:
Ever wondered if you're paying too much for your mutual funds? There are two types: regular and direct. Regular plans cost you more because someone earns a commission. Direct plans are cheaper, meaning more money stays in your pocket and grows over time! SEBI now encourages direct plans, making them easier to choose. This small change can make a big difference to your savings. Learn how in our full article.
